summary:
Filesystem ownership values are reported through the caller's user namespace. The pinned Arch Linux source converts inode IDs with from_kuid_munged/from_kgid_munged against current_user_ns; an unmapped ID becomes the configured overflow ID. Therefore namespace UID0 is not a universal host-Root identity, and accepting an overflow UID cannot distinguish hostRoot0 from another unmapped owner. A mapped UID match alone is insufficient host ownership authority. Use an authenticated host view, or independently joined host-owned inode authority with explicit mapping and original context; retain closed directory, inode and byte checks.

The concrete source-review failure appeared in a new consumer executed inside a Podman engine user namespace. It demanded host UID0/GID1000 and hostRoot directory owners using that namespace's local stat results. The immutable Root exports could be valid in the host view and still fail those checks. Root held that source despite its original passing388supervisor/56VM/58provider controls. The existing default callback refusal prevented an actual unsafe native operation. The finding is scoped to the new Root-result reader; capture-peer rows carried no claimed host UID and their later actual-host checks were not a second instance. Public review: https://github.com/FS-GG/.github/issues/4516#issuecomment-6414203189 ; complete scoped return: https://github.com/FS-GG/.github/issues/4516#issuecomment-6414268683 .

Moving the reader outside the engine does not make every reverse authentication query available. In the same pinned kernel, proc namespace readlink requires ptrace READ_FSCREDS access. The capability hook permits the same user namespace with sufficient capability coverage, or CAP_SYS_PTRACE in the target's user namespace. Root in a descendant engine namespace does not gain initial-host namespace capabilities from a matching mapped UID or Unix peer credentials. An engine client therefore cannot assume it can read an outside host observer's namespace links. Root and an independent reviewer verified this constraint from pinned source; no actual Home permission reproduction was performed. Source-backed return: https://github.com/FS-GG/.github/issues/4516#issuecomment-6414447534 .

Home's selected repair places Root ownership and namespace self-checks in the admitted original host observer, then joins its original PID/birth, boot, source, context and actual kernel peer over a credentialed channel to the bridge. The actual socket/server creation context, translated credentials and original deadlines still require coherent source and runtime evidence. An ordinary dictionary, permission fallback or namespace-FD export cannot substitute for the missing identity proof. At this capture the host-observer repair was in progress; its trusted frontend, complete runtime admission and genuine native qualification remained unassembled. Pinned kernel rules and source review do not establish deployed capability, reader/writer safety, export, bake or consumer acceptance.
title: Authenticate host ownership in the correct user namespace
